title: Citrus room spray
subtitle: A bright, fresh air freshener for kitchens and bathrooms
excerpt: A vodka-based room spray of sweet orange, lemon, and bergamot essential oils. Clears cooking smells and freshens small rooms without synthetic fragrance. Makes 100 ml.
sourceNotes: Essential-oil phototoxicity: IFRA guidelines for cold-pressed citrus oils (2020). Bergamot EO pet-safety notes: ASPCA toxic plants and substances list (aspca.org). Alcohol as dispersant in room sprays: standard cosmetic formulation reference.

recipe.batchNotes: Doubles to 200 ml in a larger bottle.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Mix and store in a labelled bottle; ready in minutes.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Keeps six months in a sealed spray bottle. Cold-pressed citrus oils oxidise and lose their bright top note after three to four months; the spray will still work but smell flatter. Discard if it smells sour or rancid.

glossaryTerms.definition: Essential oil expressed mechanically from the outer peel of citrus fruit at low temperatures. Gives a true fresh citrus scent. Oxidises faster than steam-distilled oils and should be kept away from light and heat.

content.text: room spray for kitchens, bathrooms, and hallways. Three citrus essential oils give it a sharp, fresh top note that clears cooking smells quickly. The vodka disperses the oils in the water base and extends the shelf life.
All three oils are toxic to cats. Do not spray in rooms cats frequent.

items.prepNote: distilled to avoid mineral residue in the nozzle
cold-pressed lemon peel oil; sharpens the blend
adds a light floral lift; phototoxic but safe as a room spray not touching skin

content.text: Add the essential oils to the vodka in the spray bottle and swirl to blend.
Top up with the distilled water. Fit the cap and shake.
Keeps six months. The bright citrus top note is strongest for the first three months. Shake before each use. Discard if the spray smells flat or sour.
